Order notation reference

Source: vignettes/notation.Rmd
notation.Rmd
library(diplomacyR)

Diplomacy players write orders in a compact shorthand that has been stable for decades but was never standardised. dp_parse_orders() accepts the spellings people actually use, and format() renders any dp_orders tibble back into one canonical form. This vignette is the reference for both.

Every example below is parsed and then rendered back, so the second column is what the engine understood.

notation <- function(x, ...) {
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    Written = x,
    Understood = format(dp_parse_orders(x, ...))
  ))
}

The shape of an order

An order is

Power: <unit> <verb> <arguments>

The power prefix may be dropped if the power argument supplies it instead. Everything is case-insensitive, and powers may be abbreviated to any unambiguous prefix.

notation(c(
  "France: A Par - Bur",
  "FRANCE: A Par - Bur",
  "Fra: A Par - Bur",
  "F: A Par - Bur"
))
Written Understood
France: A Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur
FRANCE: A Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur
Fra: A Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur
F: A Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur 
dp_parse_orders(c("A Par - Bur", "A Mar - Spa"), power = "France")
#> <dp_orders> (2 orders)
#> France: A Par - Bur
#> France: A Mar - Spa

Locations

Provinces are three-letter codes. Full province names are accepted too and are translated to codes.

notation(c(
  "France: A Par - Bur",
  "France: A Paris - Burgundy",
  "France: A paris to burgundy"
))
Written Understood
France: A Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur
France: A Paris - Burgundy France: A Par - Bur
France: A paris to burgundy France: A Par - Bur

Three provinces on the standard board have two coasts that a fleet cannot sail between: Spain (nc, sc), Bulgaria (ec, sc) and St Petersburg (nc, sc). Write the coast after a slash, or in brackets.

notation(c(
  "Russia: F Stp/sc - Bot",
  "Russia: F Stp (sc) - Bot",
  "Russia: F STP/SC - BOT",
  "Turkey: F Bul/ec - Bla"
))
Written Understood
Russia: F Stp/sc - Bot Russia: F Stp/sc - Bot
Russia: F Stp (sc) - Bot Russia: F Stp/sc - Bot
Russia: F STP/SC - BOT Russia: F Stp/sc - Bot
Turkey: F Bul/ec - Bla Turkey: F Bul/ec - Bla

A coast is only required where the choice is genuinely ambiguous. If exactly one coast of the destination is reachable, the engine fills it in for you when it adjudicates; if two are, the order is void and the unit holds.

Units

A and F mark armies and fleets, and the long forms army and fleet work as well. The designator is optional — the engine reads the real unit type off the board — but including it is the convention, and it makes an order set readable on its own.

notation(c(
  "France: A Par - Bur",
  "France: army Par - Bur",
  "France: Par - Bur"
))
Written Understood
France: A Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur
France: army Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur
France: Par - Bur France: Par - Bur

Holds

A unit with no verb holds. H, hold, holds, stand and stands all say the same thing explicitly.

notation(c(
  "Austria: A Bud H",
  "Austria: A Bud holds",
  "Austria: A Bud stands",
  "Austria: A Bud"
))
Written Understood
Austria: A Bud H Austria: A Bud H
Austria: A Bud holds Austria: A Bud H
Austria: A Bud stands Austria: A Bud H
Austria: A Bud Austria: A Bud H

Moves

The move arrow may be a hyphen, an arrow, a dash of any Unicode flavour, or the word to. Spaces around it are optional.

notation(c(
  "France: A Par - Bur",
  "France: A Par-Bur",
  "France: A Par -> Bur",
  "France: A Par to Bur"
))
Written Understood
France: A Par - Bur France: A Par - Bur
France: A Par-Bur France: A Par - Bur
France: A Par -> Bur France: A Par - Bur
France: A Par to Bur France: A Par - Bur

Supports

A support either backs a unit that is staying where it is, in which case only the supported unit’s province is named, or backs a move, in which case the whole move is written out. S, sup, supp, support and supports are interchangeable, and the supported unit’s own designator is optional.

notation(c(
  "England: F Lon S F Yor",
  "England: F Lon S Yor",
  "England: F Lon S A Wal - Yor",
  "England: F Lon supports A Wal - Yor"
))
Written Understood
England: F Lon S F Yor England: F Lon S F Yor
England: F Lon S Yor England: F Lon S Yor
England: F Lon S A Wal - Yor England: F Lon S A Wal - Yor
England: F Lon supports A Wal - Yor England: F Lon S A Wal - Yor

Convoys

A convoy order names the army and its full move. C, conv, convoy and convoys are interchangeable.

notation(c(
  "England: F Nth C A Lon - Nwy",
  "England: F Nth convoys A Lon - Nwy",
  "England: F Nth C Lon - Nwy"
))
Written Understood
England: F Nth C A Lon - Nwy England: F Nth C A Lon - Nwy
England: F Nth convoys A Lon - Nwy England: F Nth C A Lon - Nwy
England: F Nth C Lon - Nwy England: F Nth C Lon - Nwy

The army being convoyed is ordered to move as usual. Where the destination is not adjacent, the move is a convoy automatically. Where both a land route and a sea route exist, append via convoy — or by convoy — to insist on the sea route.

notation(c(
  "England: A Lon - Bel via convoy",
  "England: A Lon - Bel by convoy"
))
Written Understood
England: A Lon - Bel via convoy England: A Lon - Bel via Convoy
England: A Lon - Bel by convoy England: A Lon - Bel via Convoy

This is the one distinction format() preserves in the rendered output, as via Convoy, because it changes the meaning of the order.

Retreat phases

The phase argument tells the parser which kind of turn the orders belong to. In a retreat phase a bare move arrow means a retreat; R, retreat and retreats say so explicitly and work in any phase. A dislodged unit that is not retreating is removed with D, disband or remove.

notation(
  c("Austria: A Tri R Alb",
    "Austria: A Tri retreats Alb",
    "Austria: A Tri - Alb",
    "Austria: A Tri D"),
  phase = "retreat"
)
Written Understood
Austria: A Tri R Alb Austria: A Tri R Alb
Austria: A Tri retreats Alb Austria: A Tri R Alb
Austria: A Tri - Alb Austria: A Tri R Alb
Austria: A Tri D Austria: Remove A Tri

Adjustment phases

Winter orders build and remove units. Builds must name the unit type, since there is no unit on the board to read it from; removals need not.

notation(
  c("Germany: Build A Ber",
    "Germany: Build F Kie",
    "Germany: F Kie B",
    "Germany: Remove F Ber",
    "Germany: Disband A Mun",
    "Germany: A Mun",
    "Germany: Waive"),
  phase = "build"
)
Written Understood
Germany: Build A Ber Germany: Build A Ber
Germany: Build F Kie Germany: Build F Kie
Germany: F Kie B Germany: Build F Kie
Germany: Remove F Ber Germany: Remove F Ber
Germany: Disband A Mun Germany: Remove A Mun
Germany: A Mun Germany: Remove A Mun
Germany: Waive Germany: Waive

Note the last two rows. In an adjustment phase a bare A Mun is a removal, not a hold — there is nothing to hold in a winter turn. Waive declines a build that is owed, which matters when a power would rather not put a unit on the board.

A fleet built on a split-coast province names its coast the same way a move does.

notation("Russia: Build F Stp/sc", phase = "build")
Written Understood
Russia: Build F Stp/sc Russia: Build F Stp/sc

Writing several orders at once

dp_parse_orders() takes a character vector of orders, but it also splits on newlines and semicolons, so a whole turn can be pasted in as one string. Anything after a # is a comment.

dp_parse_orders(
  "A Par - Bur      # open towards Munich
   A Mar S A Par - Bur
   F Bre - Mao",
  power = "France"
)
#> <dp_orders> (3 orders)
#> France: A Par - Bur
#> France: A Mar S A Par - Bur
#> France: F Bre - Mao

Round trips

format() renders orders in one canonical spelling: power prefix, unit designator, three-letter codes with the first letter capitalised, and the single-letter verbs. Parsing the rendered text gives the same orders back.

orders <- dp_example_orders("fall_1901")
canonical <- format(orders)
head(canonical, 4)
#> [1] "Austria: A Tri H"             "Austria: A Ser - Gre"        
#> [3] "Austria: F Alb S A Ser - Gre" "England: F Nth - Nwy"
identical(format(dp_parse_orders(canonical)), canonical)
#> [1] TRUE

as.character() on a dp_orders tibble is the same as format(), and as_tibble() strips the class to expose the columns the engine actually works with.

as_tibble(dp_parse_orders("England: F Nth C A Lon - Nwy"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   power   type   unit_type loc   target aux_type aux_loc aux_target via_convoy
#>   <chr>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr> <chr>  <chr>    <chr>   <chr>      <lgl>     
#> 1 England convoy fleet     nth   NA     army     lon     nwy        FALSE

When an order cannot be read

A string that is not an order at all is an error, with the offending piece named. This is deliberate: a typo in an order set should stop the turn rather than quietly become a hold.

dp_parse_orders("France: A Par flies to Bur")
#> Error:
#> ! Could not parse the order "A Par flies to Bur".
#> ✖ "flies to bur" is not a recognised order verb.
#> ℹ Use "-" (move), "H", "S", "C", "R", "Build" or "Remove".
dp_parse_orders("France: A Xyz - Bur")
#> Error:
#> ! Could not parse the order "A Xyz - Bur".
#> ✖ Unit location "xyz" is not a province on this board.
dp_parse_orders("A Par - Bur")
#> Error:
#> ! No power given for order "A Par - Bur".
#> ℹ Prefix the order with `Power:` or set `power`.

An order that parses but breaks the rules of the board is a different matter. Those are accepted here and dealt with by the adjudicator, which converts them to holds and records why — see vignette("adjudication").
